source: JoyPro curated on the maker's photo (2026-10-12), MongoosT-50 BE grip seen from behind and the right: head face with the red button and five hats/buttons toward the viewer, front of the grip to the right (red trigger and the dark curved lever under the head tip, ribbed side switch on the head front), brake lever at the lower front, knurled grip nut at the bottom
mappingSource: catalog has no input numbers (no official button map survives; product pages https://virpil-controls.eu/vpc-mongoost-50-grip.html and https://virpil-controls.eu/vpc-mongoost-50be-grip.html list the control set). Identities taken from the product description and by analogy with the successor's official sheet (MongoosT-50CM2 grip, https://support.virpil.com/en/support/solutions/articles/47001250820-vpc-mongoost-50cm2-grip), whose head has the same layout
note: positions are sure; which catalog part each hat/button is is NOT (the catalog names them only hat.1-3 and button 1-4). Those are kept as hidden candidates (medium map=low) in a JoyPro order: hat.1 stepped square hat, hat.2 concentric hat, hat.3 ribbed face hat; thumb.1/thumb.2 the two round face buttons. The other two plain buttons and the third grip-side control sit on the far side (see gallery-3: a domed control and a round button on the grip side) and are not on this photo. hat.4 (2-position index switch) = the ribbed switch on the front side of the head, by the product description ("index-side") and the CM2 sheet, where the same spot is the side rocker 17-19. Red trigger under the head = dual-stage trigger (same place as the CM2 trigger 1/2). The dark curved lever under the head tip is likely the folding trigger, but the CM2 sheet leaves the same-looking blade unlabeled, so it stays a candidate.
